title: Three against four — Ask whether a meeting adds a note or removes a silence
summary: Try three questions about notes and meetings
lead: A slot is a place in the measure. A note belongs to a voice. Keep those two counts separate while you change the checked notes and Four’s offset.

questions.title: Are there six notes or seven?
questions.prompt: Enable all three Three notes and all four Four notes. Set Four’s offset to zero. Read the twelve-slot census before playing one measure.
questions.answer: There are seven notes at six occupied slots. Both voices enter at slot 1, so that one place holds two notes. The other five occupied slots each hold one. A shared entrance does not remove either voice.

questions.title: What does an offset move?
questions.prompt: Keep the complete pattern. Change Four’s offset from zero to one. Compare every slot with the kept measure. Where does the shared entrance go?
questions.answer: It moves from slot 1 to slot 5. Three remains at slots 1, 5 and 9; Four moves to 2, 5, 8 and 11. The kept column still uses its own offset. Seven notes remain seven notes.

questions.title: Is a missing note a softer note?
questions.prompt: Uncheck one Four note and play a finite measure. If you want a visual answer first, inspect the slot where that note used to arrive.
questions.answer: It is a rest. The removed voice does not sound at that entrance, and the remaining notes are not amplified to compensate. At a shared entrance, removing Four can leave Three there without making the slot silent.
